intro.author: Joel son of Pethuel (1:1); nothing else is known about him
intro.written: Uncertain: the book names no king, and proposals range from the 800s BC to after the exile (around 400 BC)
intro.audience: The people of Judah and Jerusalem, with their priests and elders
intro.setting: A devastating locust plague and drought had stripped Judah's fields, vines and orchards, leaving nothing even for the temple's daily offerings. Joel reads this disaster as a warning of a greater 'day of the LORD.'
intro.purpose: To call the whole nation to wholehearted repentance and to promise that God would restore the land, pour out his Spirit and judge the nations.
intro.bigIdea: 'Rend your heart, and not your garments,' because the Lord is gracious and will restore.

outline.title: The locust plague and a call to lament
The day of the LORD, repentance and restoration
Judgment on the nations and blessing for Zion
